text: Keeps one chunk working while you are far away. A relay endpoint, a Listening Pit or a gate in a distant chunk stops when nobody is near; a Wayanchor keeps its chunk loaded for **16 Pulse** a second.

pages.title: Running one
text: Place it inside the chunk that must stay awake. It holds exactly that one chunk, not a radius around it.
It keeps a reserve of **2,400 Pulse** and refills it by up to **80** a second from generators within 8. You can also top it up with a Pulse Cell.
Redstone, or an empty reserve, lets the chunk go. Breaking the anchor lets it go at once.
Right-click it to see whether it is holding. A comparator reads 15 while it is.

pages.title: Limits and uses
text: Up to **32** anchors can run in each world. Members of a [shared camp](shared_camps) instead share **12** between them, counted across every world, so agree on which chunks matter.
Relays never keep chunks loaded themselves. If both ends of a relay must work while you travel, put an anchor at the far end.
Gates hold their far end awake for a few seconds when someone arrives, so a gate needs an anchor only if something there must keep running.
